expectations_used.clarify: Pins down, from the visible cases in tests/cases_part1.json through cases_part3.json, that Part 1 guarantees exactly one valid tote pair with no self-pairing, that Part 2 caps at one voucher per lane with a separate total-vouchers budget, and that Part 3's relay may start with either truck or drone rather than a fixed carrier — instead of assuming an unstated variant of any of these.
expectations_used.approach: Names a mechanism per part before typing it: a single-pass hash map from tote weight to position for Part 1; a Dijkstra-style search whose state is (hub, vouchers spent so far) rather than hub alone for Part 2; and a layered BFS tracking (depot, next-required-carrier) rather than a single-color BFS for Part 3.
expectations_used.communicate: States which of the three files is being worked and which mechanism is being encoded as it is typed - e.g. saying that Part 2's state space needs the vouchers-spent dimension because a lane's cost depends on whether a voucher was already spent on it, and that Part 3 needs two BFS frontiers, one per next-expected-carrier - rather than going quiet through the implementation and only speaking again at submit.
expectations_used.implement: Implements solve(tote_weights, pallet_limit) without ever pairing a position with itself, solve(hub_count, lanes, vouchers) so no lane is discounted twice and the search bounds the vouchers-used dimension by vouchers, and solve(depot_count, truck_legs, drone_legs) so entry 0 of the returned array is always 0 and unreachable depots read -1.
expectations_used.verify: Before the one-shot submit, hand-traces all three solutions against their worked examples plus at least one large case from each part's cases file (e.g. the 1000-hub, 25-voucher case in Part 2, or the 15-depot alternating-cycle case in Part 3) rather than trusting the small examples alone to catch a state-space or off-by-one error at the constraint ceiling.
expectations_used.reflect: States, per part, which mechanism was used and what would break it - for example that Part 2's extra state dimension is what keeps a cheaper-but-more-discounted path from being missed, and that Part 3's alternating constraint can make a depot's answer strictly larger than its plain-BFS distance - rather than a one-line 'it passed' summary.

summary: The candidate quickly toured all three solution and test files, made a brief but accurate mechanism summary of all three parts at the end, and submitted once, passing all 36 tests. The session shows almost no narration during the actual editing work and no visible verification step before the single submit, though the final outcome was fully green.

dimensions.analysis: There is no visible moment where the candidate surfaces or resolves ambiguity about the exactly-one-pair guarantee, the per-lane voucher cap, or the either-carrier start for the relay. The session is too compressed and terse to tell whether ambiguity was silently resolved through reading or simply never engaged with.

At +208s the candidate names a mechanism for each part in a single breath - single-pass hashmap for part1, Dijkstra with a vouchers-spent state dimension for part2, alternating-carrier BFS for part3 - which is specific enough to be wrong and matches the intended approaches. However this came right before submission rather than as an evolving plan stated before touching each file, so it reads more like a summary than a plan that guided the visible work.

Aside from the single consolidated statement at +208s, the four-minute session is almost entirely silent narration-wise while files are opened, edited, and saved across all three parts. An interviewer watching the transcript would have had to interrupt repeatedly to know what was being reasoned through during the edits at +70s, +161s, and +250s.

The actual code edits are not shown in detail - only file opens, saves, and edits to solution_part3.py and tests/test_part1.py are logged without content, so it's not possible to judge whether the implementation matched the stated mechanisms (e.g. correctly bounding the vouchers dimension or handling either-carrier start) versus just superficial touches.

There is no evidence of hand-tracing against worked examples or large constraint-ceiling cases from the cases files before the one-shot submit; the candidate went straight from the summary statement at +208s to editing part3 and submitting at +269s with no intermediate test run or trace shown.

The closing statement at +208s restates the chosen mechanisms but does not explain why each mechanism is necessary or what would break without it (e.g. why the vouchers-spent dimension prevents missing a cheaper discounted path, or why alternating constraint can exceed plain BFS distance); after submission the candidate immediately ended the session with no further reflection.
